To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
NFATc 2-deficent mice older than 1 year were anemic and showed extramedullary hemotopoiesis.
NFATc1−/− mice are anemic, thrombocytogenic and develop extramedullary hemotopoiesis in old age.

NFATc-deficient mice older than 3 months were anemic, thrombocytogenic and had a markedly reduced number and differentiation potential of bone marrow cells, which was associated with ossification of bone marrow space, and development of extramedullary haematopoiesis in spleen.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel mechanism of anemia and thrombocypenia in aged mice.
the transcriptional control of hematopoiesis.
the molecular mechanisms of bone and hematopoiesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the NFATc2 protein is required for the normal function of the hematopoietic system, and its absence causes anemia, thrombocytosis and osteomyelosclerosis.
NFATc1 is required for osteoclastogenesis and that NFATc3 is required for osteoblastogenesis.
NFATc1 and NFATc2 are required in different stages of osteoclastogenesis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NFATc1 and NFATc2 play opposing roles in hematopoiesic stem cell differentiation.
NFATc 2 plays an important role in the maintenance and regulation of hematopoiesis.
NFATc1 and NFATc2 have opposite functions in the regulation of osteoblast differentiation and bone formation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
mice lacking NFATC2 are anemic and thrombotic and develop extramedullary hemopoiesis.
the absence of NFATc1 and NFATc2 results in a phenotype of osteomyelosclerosis with anemia.
NFATc4 is required for the maintenance of hematopoiesis, and its deficiency leads to a progressive anemia and thrombocopenia.
